# Design register

**Owner:** Design Director (`main-2`) · **Opened:** 2026-07-30
**States:** Exploration → Candidate → Approved (Allen) → Implemented → Design-verified

One line per item. Built from the three slices' own packages, not from the charter's summary.
Paths are worktree-relative: `[ST]` = `surething-ui`, `[RM]` = `room-refinement`, `[TV]` = `tv-sweat`,
`[M2]` = `main-2`.

**Nothing in the studio is Design-verified yet.** No implementation has been through design review
under this seat. That is the gap this register exists to close.

Standing structure: across-time regression baseline = ROW NUMBERS, authored form (deal-invariant, exact); within-frame legibility (clause 2) = both groups, measured form, one frame only. Two jobs, two groups, two forms — one number spanning all of it is why ~0.037 could not be right for any of it. Cost nothing by luck, not design. Phone baseline (0.567, PHONEREF01/msgs-03) noted deal-dependent with NO invariant subgroup — never compared across time at another seed. Part A endorsed as the C37 characterization this instrument never had |

| S73 | Presenting a same-game ticket's price honestly, against a board of multipliable odds | **RULED** · DD 2026-08-12 batch 45, on the SGP lane's step-1 recommendation (`docs/sgp/`, `bbd67e6`). **The lane re-put the question correctly** — correct pricing LENGTHENS 78.07% of two-leg tickets, so the problem is not shortening but **INCONSISTENCY**: the shapes players most want to build are the ones that shorten (~32% at three legs, ρ median 1.63) while a corners-and-cards ticket lengthens, so no stable rule forms and the only available intuition (*related legs pay less*) is wrong for most tickets. **The diagnosis: TWO EFFECTS ARE SUPERIMPOSED and the surface shows only their sum** — (1) **correlation**, where related legs add less risk than they appear to and the ticket shortens, and (2) **vig**, where the naive product charges margin once per leg while the joint charges it once, lengthening everything. **The player cannot learn the rule because he sees one number containing both, and only one of the two is something he can act on.** **RULED, seven clauses.** **(1) A same-game ticket is its OWN INSTRUMENT, never a parlay with an adjustment — the surface NEVER displays a product-of-legs figure for it, and never an adjustment, a correlation discount, a was/now, or any deduction line.** This does the most work, so the reasoning is on the record: **the nerf reading is manufactured by the comparison and the comparison is manufactured by showing the product** — a surface printing *1.85 × 2.10 × 3.40 = 13.21, adjustment −32%, price 8.98* has **literally rendered a number being taken away from the player**, and no copy fixes that. There is nothing to deduct from if nothing is presented to deduct from; a same-game ticket is one bet on one compound outcome and it has A PRICE. **(2) The relationship is MARKED, in the house's own ink, which already means this:** oxide is *the house acting on the document* (S3, S15's strike its worked case) and biro is *what the player chose* — **the player picks his legs in biro, the house marks the connection between them in oxide.** Nothing is invented; this is the existing ink law doing the job it was written for, and it is the identity of the surface — **a correlation IS an annotation**, and the machine noticing that two legs tell one story is the most in-character thing this product could do with the fact. It also solves learnability with no formula: the rule becomes **"legs the house has marked pay less"**, which is true, visible and actionable. **(3) The LENGTHENING is not remarked** — no badge, no *better value*, no flag; a product congratulating itself for charging less is exhortation in the register T27 and S45 both closed. Silence is not concealment, because per clause 1 nothing ever claimed the price was a product. **(4) THE DIAL CONSTRAINT ON STEP 2, which binds pricing rather than presentation: any ticket priced materially shorter than the naive product must carry a relationship the surface can NAME.** Shortening a ticket whose relatedness cannot be marked charges the player for something he cannot see at the point of spending — **S17's class exactly**. **So the correlation model must expose a NAMEABLE RELATION, not only a scalar ρ**; the dial stays free in magnitude and is **constrained in kind**. Two costs to carry now rather than discover at step 5: the model emits a **relation label** beside its joint probability (enough to compose a sentence, not enough to be a formula), and **where it finds correlation it cannot label, the price does not move** — a deliberate constraint on pricing. **(5) Impossible combinations are refused at the slip, in words, once** — **not a disabled control** (S24 bans the disabled state outright; S56 bans a distinction in a channel the player cannot see); the leg stays reachable alone so **C19 is untouched** (the engine prices the leg, it refuses to price the COMBINATION); the refusal states the fact in the house's ink — *these two cannot both land*. **A bet that cannot win must never be purchasable:** a price is a factual claim about an outcome, and selling a finite price on an impossible event is the product lying in the one place it promised not to. **(6) An implication leg SAYS SO** — for the 22 implication shapes the second leg moves the price by roughly the margin alone, and **a leg that lands and changes nothing reads as broken and teaches a false rule**; the surface states it in the machine's voice (*this adds nothing; the first leg already contains it*), which is the same annotation channel as clause 2 and the most characterful moment in the feature. **(7) No formulae on the face** — T21's principle: values appear when the sim emits them as first-class, never computed in presentation; no ρ, no multiplier, no percentage is ever printed. **COUPLING TO ALLEN'S CALL #1, named because the lane's four questions are not independent: clause 2 is what destroys the exploit as a discoverable mechanic**, since preserving it would require the surface to HIDE the connection and clause 4's problem then returns with no remedy. **The design side of that decision, which the lane did not make: the exploit exists only under INCORRECT pricing, and incorrect pricing here means selling tickets that CANNOT WIN at finite odds up to a mean decimal of 2070.70.** That is not a discoverable mechanic — a price is a fact, and **S45 is the standing law that satire never occupies a slot where a fact belongs**. Recommended to Allen: price honestly, move the exploit to relics, **where a relic breaking a book the player has learned to trust is worth far more than a bug found in a book that was never correct**. **FLAGGED NOT RULED — the instrument needs a name:** if it is its own instrument it needs its own word and **`SGP` is industry jargon** against S22's vocabulary law; `SAME MATCH` is the obvious direction and is a fact rather than a brand — **material naming is Allen's** (S16, S46 both his), raised now so step 2 does not bake `SGP` into player-facing strings. **TV CONSEQUENCE noted, not ruled:** a same-game ticket's legs appear in the TV ticket column during the sweat and **the mark must survive that trip or the two surfaces disagree about what the ticket is**; TV's leg rows are ruled at T24/T40/G1 with its own ink register, so how the mark renders there is TV's question — scheduled rather than discovered, and it does not block step 2 **S73-am · batch 46 — Q1/Q2/Q3 ruled on the lane's sharper brief, DRAWS-AWARE; batch 45's DIAGNOSIS is superseded and every ruling in it survives on stronger ground.** **The diagnosis first:** batch 45 built the learnability problem on *two superimposed effects* — correlation shortening, **vig lengthening everything** — which was correct for the state in `step-1-recommendation.md` (78.07% lengthen at `Ω_sgp = Ω`). **The ADOPTED margin rule removes the vig half:** `shown price ÷ product = 1/ρ`, so **51.4% of two-leg tickets are exactly independent and price IDENTICALLY to the multiplied number.** Recorded as a **moving input, not a misreading** — the dial was set after the document ruled on — and the consequence is that **the divergence is no longer a mixture but a clean signal appearing ONLY where correlation exists**, which is the condition clause 4 was written to require. **One thing gets harder and is named: intermittent correctness teaches a habit more strongly than uniform divergence** — the player multiplies, is **exactly right 51.4% of the time**, then is silently wrong by ~39% on the shapes he most wants to build; a rule that works half the time is learned as a rule that works. **Q1 — RULED: the qualitative marker, option 3, no arithmetic.** Not *show nothing* (the brief makes the case itself — a player who multiplies and finds a discrepancy has found a REAL one and deserves an answer; silence is **S17's class**). Not *show both numbers* — it makes the slip a calculator (**T21**), renders the same fact twice (**S58**), and puts a number visibly moving on the document; it would not always be a deduction, since negatively correlated tickets pay MORE, but a two-directional correction line is **worse**, teaching the player to watch a number change rather than read his ticket. **What the mark buys is the whole argument: the player's complete and CORRECT mental model needs no arithmetic — *unmarked legs multiply; marked legs pay less*.** The mark is what **makes** the multiplication rule work rather than what replaces it, telling him exactly when his own arithmetic applies. **The fairness fact is NOT printed:** the brief offers that a same-game ticket carries the same house edge as an equivalent cross-game parlay and that this is defensible — it is true, and it stays off the slip, because **a house that explains its own fairness at the point of spending reads as a house with something to explain** (S44's boundary — the machine does not wear the house's brand, and the house does not testify about itself on the player's document). **Q2 — RULED: WARN. Not block, not silence.** **Silence refused outright** — the brief's own *"quietly milked by a trap they cannot see"* is **S17 verbatim**, and it is the most corrosive thing available to a product whose promise is that the numbers do not lie. **Blocking refused, and NOT on paternalism, which is the weaker argument: a redundant leg is a LEGAL bet, correctly priced.** This game is about a player learning to read a book — **a house that prevents you from being stupid is not this product; a house that tells you and lets you do it anyway is exactly this product** — and blocking forecloses uses nobody has anticipated (a relic, a challenge condition). **The clutter objection dissolves:** the warning appears on **22 shapes**, not on every slip. Copy states the fact naming both legs — *`OVER 1.5 GOALS adds nothing — OVER 2.5 GOALS already contains it`* — **and it is the most credible thing in the feature because it costs the house money to say**, which is what makes the rest of the machine believable. **Q3 — RULED DRAWS-AWARE; the trap does not partially dissolve, it GOES.** Allen greenlit draws today, and **both artefact shapes were impossible only because 1–1 was unrepresentable** — with draws, `BTTS YES + Under 2.5` is a legal, ordinary, popular ticket; not refused, no copy written, nothing left to expose. **STANDING RULE, bigger than the two shapes: the surface refuses only what is impossible in FOOTBALL, never what is merely impossible in the MODEL; where the model is more restrictive than the game it simulates, the MODEL is the defect and the refusal does not ship.** **Why it is a law and not a copy preference: a refusal is the machine making a factual claim about the world**, and if it says *these cannot both happen* about something real football does every weekend, a football-literate player catches the product lying — **and every other number the machine shows loses its credit at the same moment. This surface's authority is that it does not lie about facts, and that authority is indivisible.** It generalises past draws, since any v1 simplification manufactures the same false refusals: **before a refusal ships it is checked against football, not against the model**, and the check states what it could not cover (C18 §4.2). **STEP-3 CONSEQUENCE, the build reach the brief predicted: the impossible set is RE-DERIVED after draws land** — the 22 two-leg and 57 three-leg shapes were enumerated against a drawless model and that enumeration is now stale **in the direction that matters, over-refusing**; every shape re-checked, the two known artefacts expected to leave. **The refusal reads:** *`OVER 2.5 GOALS and UNDER 1.5 GOALS cannot both land`* — the fact, both legs named, once, at the slip in its own space; **not a modal** (S55), **not a disabled control** (S24, S56), no scolding (S71/S72 — name the state, not the owner). It teaches because it is **specific**: the player learns which two legs conflict, which is real football knowledge he keeps. **THE INK SPLIT, stated because three annotations now exist and will otherwise be muddled: OXIDE for the correlation link** (the house's mark ON the player's picks — S3's own definition, the dead-leg strike's family); **TONER for both statements** — *adds nothing* and *cannot both land* — (the machine stating a fact in its own space, S26's *state rather than exhort*); **BIRO for none of them, ever**, biro being only what the player chose, with S26 the worked case of getting exactly this wrong. The distinction that keeps oxide from diluting: **oxide marks the house acting on his picks; toner is the machine saying something true — a refusal is not the house acting, it is arithmetic, spoken** **S73-am2 · batch 47 — ALLEN'S DECISION: THE HONEST BOOK IS YES.** The coupling named at S73 resolves in the direction recommended — **the mark ships, the exploit dies.** Clause 2 is unblocked and step 2 proceeds under clause 4's constraint: the model emits a **relation label** beside its joint, and **where it cannot label a correlation the price does not move.** **Consequence ROUTED, not executed:** `02-betting-math.md:24` carries the *"correlated parlay as discoverable exploit"* framing and that framing is now dead — it is a **shared canonical document, edited at integration and not by this seat** (STUDIO.md's ownership rule), so it is named as an owed edit rather than made; the replacement is on the record at S73, **the exploit moves to relics, where a relic breaking a book the player has learned to trust is worth more than a bug found in a book that was never correct.** **STILL ALLEN'S AND STILL OPEN: the mark's name**, held for him as is the instrument's (`SGP` is jargon against S22; `SAME MATCH` offered as the direction) — **named here so step 2 bakes neither into player-facing strings**, and the build can proceed on placeholders since neither name changes a mechanism **S73-am3 · batch 48 — ALLEN'S TWO NAMES, INTO CANON: the instrument is `SAME MATCH`; the mark is `THE HOUSE'S LINE`. Player-facing strings may be authored REAL from this line — no placeholders on either.** **Why the mark's name is better than the brief that asked for it, recorded because the lane builds against it: `THE HOUSE'S LINE` is true in BOTH registers at once** — it is *literally* a line the house draws on the document connecting two of the player's picks, and *"the line"* is already the betting word for what the book says. **The name is simultaneously the physical mark and the house's position, which is exactly what the mark is** — the annotated-form-guide identity in three words, arriving with nothing to explain. It sits correctly against **S3** (oxide is *the house's mark*): the mark now has a name that says whose it is, in the surface's vocabulary rather than the industry's. **RULED, because recording a name without ruling where it appears leaves the lane to guess and the wrong guess is specific and likely — `THE HOUSE'S LINE` printed beside the mark on every slip. THE MARK IS DRAWN, NOT CAPTIONED.** That would be **the house captioning its own annotation** — the move already refused at Q1 for the fairness fact, and **S44's boundary again: the machine does not narrate the house's presence on the player's document**; a mark needing a label on every occurrence is also a mark that is not working. **(1) The oxide line is drawn and carries NO LABEL** — it connects the picks and says what it says. **(2) Where a statement is needed it states the RELATION, not the name** — S73 clause 4 already requires the model to emit a relation label *"enough to compose a sentence"*, and this is that sentence: **what the legs SHARE**, in toner, in the machine's voice, once per slip, never announcing the apparatus. **(3) `THE HOUSE'S LINE` is what the thing is CALLED** — used where the product refers to it (rules copy, the ledger, a first-encounter explanation) and **never as a per-occurrence caption.** **The onboarding gap is real and is answered by the STATEMENT, not the name:** the first time a player sees an oxide line he cannot decode it (S56's class), and **the toner sentence is what teaches it, on the slip where it happens, in the same breath as the mark** — the name is how he refers to it afterwards. **`SAME MATCH` form:** uppercase as the surface's market vocabulary already is (`OVER 2.5 GOALS`, `MUSKRATS ML`), **a role printed as a word** per S22's own requirement, a fact rather than a brand; tracking follows the laptop's label treatment under `surething-design.md` §4.3 with **the token the kit's to supply, not this seat's to invent** (S70's endorsed precedent — leave it untracked rather than guess). **Nothing else moves: both names are VOCABULARY, and neither changes a mechanism, a price, a refusal, or a mark's ink** — S73 and S73-am stand exactly as ruled **S73-am4 · batch 55 — THE OWNING-DOC FOLD SURFACED A CONFLICT AND THE OWNING DOC WINS (§1.2): the impossibility refusal takes STAMP, not toner, and must carry CAUSE AND REMEDY.** Batch 46's ink split put both statements in toner on the reasoning that *a refusal is not the house acting, it is arithmetic spoken*. **`surething-design.md` §3.3 already rules the state**: **Blocked = muted label + STAMPED literal reason ≥13px, CAUSE AND REMEDY, inside the control** — and **a refused leg combination IS a Blocked state**, so it takes the treatment the surface already has rather than a new one. **Two corrections, both this seat's: (1) the ink** — Stamp, not toner, because the house declining to take a bet is the house acting on the document, which is Stamp's own definition; **(2) the copy** — batch 46's `X and Y cannot both land` gives the CAUSE only, where this row has always required **cause AND remedy**, so the refusal also names what to drop. **Constitution §1.2 decides it without argument** — the owning document outranks the register's ruling for that item on that surface's content — and **§6's *a clause that contradicts an owning document is a conflict to escalate, not a licence* is why this surfaced at the fold rather than in a build.** **UNCHANGED and re-confirmed against the doc: the implication warning is NOT a Blocked state and does NOT take Stamp** — a legal-but-pointless leg is legal, correctly priced and added, and the machine states the fact **in toner, in its own space**; The moneyline is 1X2*). **The engine fact that decides it: `MatchResult {Home, Draw, Away}` while `Side` STAYS TWO-VALUED as a TEAM designator, and `Pick.Side`/`Leg.Side` now THROW on Draw. The draw is NOT a team** — the engine ruled that structurally and **the surface must not undo it in presentation**; a draw rendered as a third team is a category error the code has already refused. **S24 predicted this exact moment** (*paired pricing describes two-outcome markets; scorer renders as a single-column offer list, never a paired row with a dead cell*): **the moneyline is no longer a two-outcome market**, so the paired row no longer describes it and must not be forced to. **RULED: three offers, the draw in the MIDDLE** — its position is not borrowed convention but **meaning**: the draw sits between the two teams because it is the outcome where **neither wins**, and putting it at either end would make it look like a third competitor, which is exactly what `Side` refuses to let it be. **Named as what it is — `DRAW` — never as a team and never with a team's treatment: no pitch dot** (T2 gives muted blue and pink to the two sides; a draw has no side and takes no hue), no crest, nothing team-coloured. **`1X2` NEVER REACHES THE PLAYER** — industry jargon exactly as `SGP` was, and **S22 governs**: the surface composes and the role is printed as a word; `1X2` is a code word for a market shape and stays in the code. **G1's DECK OWES A DRAW FORM AND THIS IS THAT AUTHORING** — G1's scope line said *a seventh market needs a form authored before it ships*, and while the draw is not a seventh market but a **third outcome on an existing one**, the moneyline's authored forms **assume a team** (`MIDDLEMEN ML`) and a draw leg has none. **The word already exists on this surface: T62 records the live leg reading `LEVEL 0–0 at 14`, so `LEVEL` is already the product's word for a tied scoreline** — nothing is invented. **NEED** (requirement, while live) = `LEVEL AT FULL TIME`; | C44 | A bound and the reading it judges must come from one instrument | **Law (register-level, C43's standing — not a constitutional amendment)** · DD 2026-08-11 batch 37: **a bound and the reading compared against it must be produced by the same instrument, in the same stated space, and a gate demonstrates this by printing both.** *Founding case:* **V6** — bound in CIELAB, reading in HSV, the two regions **DISJOINT**, and both of the gate's own founding colours failing its own band; every verdict it ever issued was void in both directions and nothing in the pipeline was positioned to notice. *Second and third catches, inside one fortnight:* this seat's own batch-36 T65 target (an authored value ruled against a rendered band — T65-am2), and the room lane's twice-paid region-comparison error, which room names in its own T65 record. **Relation to C33-am3:** that clause requires every measurement to state its space and it governed REVIEW PROSE — **V6 stated nothing and nothing required it to**, because the clause never reached a gate's own output, which is where the comparison actually happens. C44 puts it there. **The cheap test, promoted from room's own method: feed a bound the values it was derived from; if they fail, the gate is reading a different quantity than its bounds describe.** It costs one run, needs no frames, and is the only check in this family that catches a **disjoint** band rather than a merely loose one — a shifted band still passes its own founding values, a disjoint one cannot. **Standing practice: any gate carrying a numeric bound runs its founding values through itself once, and records the result beside the bound** **V6-am · batch 51 — THE BAND'S TOP IS WITHDRAWN, and this seat installed it wrongly (§1.5); V6's BOUNDS are void with it.** Room's R23 pair (`38c44da`) fired **disposition 3**: the anchors do not separate — **the high anchor reads 101.4 against a recorded ~92, a 9.4° miss on a 7° band** — and the subject was correctly **not reported as conforming**. **The find is decisive: two independent computations agree and both disagree with the record** — the key tube's **authored** colour computes **102.7°**, its **rendered** contribution measures **101.4°**, they agree within **1.3°**, and the recorded top carries **no stated derivation at all**. **That is C44's founding shape applied to a BAND rather than a gate: feed a bound its own founding value and it fails.** **§1.5 — THE NUMBER WAS ON THE RECORD AT BATCH 37, INSIDE THE TRACE THIS SEAT ACCEPTED IN FULL.** V6's own row reads *computation — CIELAB lands within 1.9° on the lid and **10.7° on the key***, and **92 + 10.7 = 102.7, exactly the authored figure measured today**. This seat **read a 10.7° miss on a 7°-wide band as CONFIRMATION that the band was correctly drawn** — a miss larger than the band is not agreement, it is the anchor saying it is not there. **Two errors, one cause:** those gaps were also re-labelled *the authored↔rendered gap*, which they never were — they are **record↔computation** gaps, the true authored↔rendered gap on the key being **1.3°**. Both mistakes are the same act, **attributing a discrepancy to the wrong pair of quantities — exactly what C44 was written to prevent, one batch after this seat wrote it.** **THE THREE-BATCH CHAIN, RECORDED STRAIGHT: batch 36's INSTINCT WAS RIGHT and its remedy wrong** — it restated the band to 83–85° reasoning that *the upper half brackets no measured member*, and the upper half indeed bracketed none, **because the real member sits ABOVE the band rather than below its top**; **batch 37 rejected 36's remedy correctly and then installed a provenance that did not exist**, restoring a top the trace in front of it was contradicting. **Batch 36 deserves the credit its correction took away — it detected the defect.** **RULED: the recorded ~92 is WITHDRAWN, and this seat DECLINES to install 101.4 in its place** — because **the choice of the key tube as the upper anchor is itself underived**, having entered the same way ~92 did, and moving the number without deriving the membership **repeats the exact defect one number later**, leaving the register carrying its third unsourced band top in three batches. **THE BAND IS RE-DERIVED ONCE, and the derivation states: (1) every MEMBER NAMED** (C18 §4.1) with its value, its **space** (CIELAB on linear, C33-am3), whether it is **authored or rendered**, and the surface or frame it was taken on; **(2) whether the key tube and the screen emitters are ONE POPULATION AT ALL** — the screens cluster tightly (lid 85.1–85.3, phone 85.4, laptop 84.3, a representative warm emission 83.3) while **the key sits ~16° above all of them**, and **a band spanning a tight cluster plus one distant member is either two populations or a bound so loose it certifies nothing**, which changes every verdict the band will ever issue; **(3) C44's OWN PRACTICE run and recorded beside the bound** — the founding values through the band once — **which had it run when C44 was ruled would have surfaced this immediately, V6 being C44's own founding case**, so the practice was written and not applied to the gate that produced it (recorded as a process finding, not a new law). **DIRECTION OFFERED, EXPLICITLY NOT A RULING:** the settlement re-tint is a **light event**, so the comparison class is the room's warm **LIGHT**, which is the key — the screens being objects lit by it rather than members of the same population; if that holds, a light event is judged against lights and the screen cluster is a different band answering a different question. **The derivation decides this; this seat is naming the fork, not taking it.** **V6's OWN BOUNDS ARE VOID WITH THE TOP:** V6 was repaired by converting its READING to CIELAB while its **bounds stayed 85–92**, so **that repair is incomplete and V6 is still mis-calibrated, now in a new way** — it takes the re-derived band before issuing another verdict; **its converted reading stands, only the bound moves** **V6-am2 · batch 52 — THE BAND, RE-DERIVED. The fork is answered: they are NOT one population and never were.** **Every member named, rendered CIELAB on linear (C33-am3), from the register's own rows:** `ArtIndicator` **49.7°** chroma 5.4 (R41 b16–17, standby lamp under **room-rust law**); `WindowGlow` **77.0°** (R42 b15, **textured emitter — the map governs**); representative warm emission **83.3°** (T65-am); laptop **84.3°**/5.3 and phone **85.4°**/5.0 (R39 b15); laptop lid **85.1–85.3°** (S63-am2 b13); **warm key tube 101.4° rendered / 102.7° authored** (room, `38c44da`). **THE ORIGIN OF ~92 IS NOW VISIBLE IN THE RECORD:** S63-am2, batch 13, reads *room cast 355.7°→85.1° **vs the key's 92°*** — **a passing comparison inside a note about the laptop lid**, never a derivation, never a measurement of the key, never given a space, **which then became a band edge by being cited. That is the whole provenance, and it is why it had none.** **THE FORK, ANSWERED: the spread is 49.7° to 101.4° — 52° wide — which is not a family but FOUR KINDS OF OBJECT measured with one instrument.** **The screens are one family and a tight one** (83.3 / 84.3 / 85.1–85.3 / 85.4, about **2° wide**) and tight **by construction**, R39 having closed them on a **shared base** (`Amp(1/3/15)` off `LaptopScreen.GrantedLidEmission`) — they are unified because one constant makes them so. **`WindowGlow` is a PICTURE, not a palette member** — R42 ruled the authored value a **multiplier** with the **emission map governing**, so its 77.0° is the night-city sodium texture and not a colour anyone chose; **nothing about it is authored as a hue, so it cannot be a band member.** **`ArtIndicator` is ratified rust law** at 49.7°. **And the key tube is the room's LIGHT** — every other member is an object IN the room; the key is what lights them. **RULED: the 83–85° band is the SCREENS' family — correct, well-founded, and the key tube was NEVER a member of it. The phantom top was A LIGHT SOURCE APPENDED TO A FAMILY OF SCREENS**, a category error, and **the same error this lane has now paid for three times in other forms** (authored-vs-rendered, HSV-vs-CIELAB, record-vs-computation) — **comparing across populations is this lane's signature defect and it produced the band's top.** **WHICH POPULATION THE SUBJECT BELONGS TO:** `RoomSettlementGlow()` paints **light into the room** — not a screen, not a texture, not an object — so **its comparison class is the room's warm LIGHT, the key.** **Consequence: the subject was never in the screens' band's jurisdiction at all**, and every verdict judging it against 83–85 or 85–92 was **judging a light event against a family of screens.** **THE BOUND: reference SOURCED, tolerance OWED, and not invented here.** The reference is **the key's rendered 101.4°**, sourced two independent ways agreeing within 1.3° — unlike `~92`. **A one-member population gives a POINT, not a band**, so a tolerance is required and has no derivation yet; **its BASIS is ruled and its NUMBER is not: floor = the instrument's demonstrated spread on this subject**, since a bound tighter than the instrument's own spread cannot fail for what it exists to catch (**C32's founding shape**). **Room reported that spread as *77% of band* — a percentage of a band that is now void — and it is needed IN DEGREES: a restatement of data already in hand, NOT a capture, no window required.** Anything tighter than that floor needs a **perceptual** basis nobody has measured, and **inventing one would be the third unsourced number on this band in four batches** **V6-am3 · batch 53 — THE GATE CHECKS A VALUE AGAINST ITS OWN FIXTURE FAMILY, NOT AGAINST ONE ROOM-WIDE BAND.** A single band across four fixture families was always going to be **either too loose to catch anything or wrong for three of them — and it was both.** **Ruled: V6 checks each value against its own family's bound**, the families being named at T65-cl with their values and provenance; **a value belonging to NO family is not gate-able by a family bound** and is ruled at this seat against the property, which is what T65-cl did. **STANDING, promoted from room's line because it is the general form: A BOUND IS DEFENDED BY THE REASONING THAT GROUPS ITS MEMBERS, NEVER BY HOW TIGHTLY THEY HAPPEN TO CLUSTER.** Clustering is evidence that a grouping **might** exist; it is never the grouping's justification. **Four batches on this band, and every wrong turn — the phantom top, the lights-vs-screens carve, the cross-population comparisons — came from treating PROXIMITY as MEMBERSHIP** | batch 37 |
| C45 | A freeze is checked against the seat's own OUTPUT, not only the lane's input | **Law (register-level, C39/C42/C43's standing — not proposed for the constitution)** · DD 2026-08-12 batch 38: where a freeze protects a verification pair, a routed **measurement** respects it by construction — measurements move no pixels and a lane reporting one is correctly freeze-clean. **The RULING that measurement produces may not be.** The freeze check therefore runs **at the moment of ruling, on what the ruling causes to change**, and **it is this seat's to run because the lane cannot see it**: from inside the lane the submission is freeze-clean and stays that way right up until someone rules on it. **Two founding cases, one batch apart, two different lanes:** **T80-am** — room's T65 settlement-cast measurement, where room stated the freeze was respected and that was true of a measurement and stopped being true when the measurement became a ruling that re-authored a value inside the pair's own frames; and **T82 / T80-am2** — TV's tabular measurement, identical shape, freeze-clean as a finding and a frozen variable the moment option (a) was granted. **Standing practice: any ruling issued while a verification pair is open states, IN THE RULING, whether it creates a frozen variable.** Two independent founding cases is what makes this a law at all; a third argues for promotion to constitution §4 beside the other instrument clauses | batch 38 |
| C46 | A fixed box carries an unstated assumption about the face it was sized against | **Law (register-level, C39/C42/C43's standing — not proposed for the constitution)** · DD 2026-08-12 batch 41, promoted from TV's structural reading of T84's sweep. **Where a layout FIXES a box's width rather than deriving it from content, that box carries an implicit claim — that the longest string it can hold fits, IN THE FACE IT WAS SIZED AGAINST. The claim is never written down, and a change of face, weight, tracking or figure set invalidates every such box at once: silently, and everywhere, because nothing in the box refers to the face it assumed.** Two consequences, both exercised: **(1) sweep the POPULATION, not the suspects** — after any change to type metrics the set at risk is *every fixed box*, not the ones a reader can think of; T84's three founding instances were found by eye in two of nine moments, and the structural reading found the class. **(2) The test is the longest RENDERABLE form, not the current content** — a box passes on what is in it today and fails on the string nobody captured. **Founding case:** Phase T, where a wider canon face produced a truncation (`ONE TEAM BLANKED` to `ONE TEAM`), a collision (`CASH OUT $131OLD E`) and a solo clipping (`MARKET SUSPENDED`) from **the same unstated assumption in three unrelated boxes**. **Retrospective fit, named as retrospective and NOT counted as founding:** S68 on the laptop, the SKIP ROUND headroom collapsing 45 px to 7 px when tracking landed at the wrong value — same shape, a fixed box and a metric change, one surface over. **Relation to the neighbours:** constitution §3.5 says *a bound is not a layout*, obliging the dependent layout to be re-derived; **C46 is its converse and its harder half — a fixed box IS a bound, an implicit one, and nobody re-derives what they never noticed they declared.** R30's *a locked band is not headroom* is the same family and already binds all three surfaces' fixed canvases, which is why this sits cross-surface rather than in TV's table. **Promotes to the constitution on a second INDEPENDENT founding case**; this seat is not counting a retrospective attribution as one **C46-am · batch 56 — A BOX SIZED BEFORE A LAW CANNOT SATISFY IT BY ACCIDENT.** C46 ruled that a fixed box carries an unstated assumption about **the face it was sized against**; the same box carries a second, **about the SET OF OBLIGATIONS its control had when the box was drawn.** **Every correct ruling that adds a required element to a control — a cost, a contract, an instruction, a state — makes that control's box worse**, and four consecutive rulings did it on one surface. **This is not evidence the rulings are wrong; it is the boxes encoding an older contract.** **Consequence, worth having in advance: when a ruling adds an element to a control, the box's fit is RE-DERIVED IN THE SAME BREATH AS THE RULING** — not discovered by a sweep two batches later — and the ruling **states whether it expects the box to still hold, saying so where it cannot tell.** **And the remedy is usually COMPOSITION, not span:** a control that has acquired a fourth obligation is rarely fixed by widening, but by admitting it now has more than one row's worth of things to say — **three instances on one surface in one pass** (the intervention prompt, `TakeoverSub`, the money control), all answered by **N independent strings are not one row** **C46-am2 · batch 58 — THE TWO SWEEP DIRECTIONS ARE COUPLED, and this is TV's finding.** T89-C required both directions on the reasoning that *nothing about the over-generation catch bounds the opposite direction*; **TV found something better — they are not independent.** **An over-generated string is only harmless when it is NOT the maximum. When it IS the maximum it sets the certified worst case, every producible form beneath it is never reached, and it therefore CONCEALS exactly the under-generation the other direction is looking for — so the two directions cannot be swept separately, and finding one does not clear the other.** **Founding case, both halves on one slot:** `BRICKLAYERS ANYTIME` was unproducible **and** the widest member of its set, so removing it did not merely delete a phantom — **it UNCOVERED that both generated arms had been swept against a hand-picked champion**, and that `LegRowNeed0` had been certified **17.5px BETTER than it is** (272.4 → 289.9). **That direction is invisible in frames by construction**, which is why it was the condition this seat cared most about, and **it fired.** **Two further shapes from the same report: the CODE KNEW the worst case and the sweep did not use it** — the construction site's own comment names `GRAVEDIGGERS TO WIN` as over budget, and **a worst case documented in a comment beside the generator is not a worst case the generator uses**; and **a form from the NEIGHBOURING SLOT had been certified against this one's box** (`MIDDLEMEN ML` in `LegRowNeed0`, where `ML` is the LINE slot's vocabulary), so **a worst case must come from the slot's OWN vocabulary, not from a plausible string.** **The remedy is the durable part and is adopted as the standard: CHAMPIONS ARE RETIRED** — the sweep **generates every producible form over the closed pools** (20 club nouns, 12 surnames, both arms each, plus authored constants and both fallbacks verbatim from their construction sites), so **a name added to either pool can no longer be missed by a champion nobody re-picked** — R16's hard-coded list of five materials, one instrument over | batch 41 |
| C47 | The match has three outcomes; a bet has two | **Law, cross-surface** · DD 2026-08-12 batch 49. Sited here rather than in a surface table because it governs **both owning documents' settlement language**, and a cross-surface law transcribed into a surface's table is invisible to anyone reading the laws end-to-end — **C43's founding defect, now seen twice.** **A draw is a third MATCH outcome. It is NOT a third BET outcome. Result language needs no third word: a leg either landed or it did not.** **Ruled: back the draw and it draws — you WON; back a team and it draws — you LOST.** Two words still cover every bet that can be placed, and **S23's enum (PENDING · RIDING · LIVE · GREEN · DEAD · VOID · CASHED OUT) is UNCHANGED and needs nothing added.** **What this prevents, and why it is a law rather than an answer: inventing a `DREW` leg state would be MODELLING THE MATCH INSIDE THE BET'S VOCABULARY** — a category error, and **the same one `Side` already refuses in the engine.** A leg has no opinion about how the match ended; it knows only whether its condition held. **The one legitimate neighbour, named so it is not mistaken for a counter-example:** a market that RETURNS THE STAKE on a draw (draw-no-bet's family) is a **VOID**, which the enum already carries — that is a different market's rule, never a third result. **Laptop echo, ruled by the same line: slip settlement language does not change** — no new word, no new state, no new column | batch 49 |
| C48 | A control's copy is its input contract | **Law, cross-surface** · DD 2026-08-12 batch 50, promoted from T88 and extending T59 to the gesture axis. **Where a control's label names a GESTURE, that gesture is what the input implements — the label is not a description of the control, it is the contract the player acts on.** T59 ruled the availability axis (*display state and input state are the same state, read from one value*); **this is the same law where the input is not merely available or refused but SHAPED** — held, pressed, released. **A label naming a SAFETY PROPERTY the input does not provide is the most dangerous copy a control can carry**, because it is relied upon precisely when the player is being careless, and because the reliance is invisible until the moment it costs him. **Founding case:** the TV's intervention prompt printing `HOLD` over a `wasPressedThisFrame` input that **committed an irreversible spend on the first frame** — no preview, no abandon path, on a surface the player is watching rather than operating (T88). **Corollary, ruled with it: the weight of the gesture matches the weight of the act.** An irreversible spend is never one frame of input; an action that costs nothing and is already the default may be. **The repair direction is fixed and it is the non-obvious half:** where copy and input disagree on a money control, **the INPUT is corrected to match the copy, not the copy to match the input** — correcting the word ships an honest description of an unsafe control, which is worse than either half alone. **Binds all four surfaces**, every one of which has controls whose labels name gestures | batch 50 |
| C49 | Money the player can win or lose is printed in FULL | **Law, cross-surface** · DD 2026-08-13 batch 57, the abbreviation ruling owed at T74-am3. Sited cross-surface because **money precision is a PRODUCT property, not a surface one** — the laptop's ledger, tallies and verdict figures are governed by the same sentence as the theatre's payout. **A money figure the player can win, lose, stake or be paid is printed in full: every digit, no abbreviation, no rounding, no `k`, no `M`, no cap.** **Three refusals, each on its own ground rather than on taste: (1) abbreviation discards precision on the one fact his money depends on, and it does so ONLY FOR LARGE NUMBERS — so it degrades exactly the wins that matter most**; `PAYS $12.3k` is not a payout, it is a description of one. **(2) A format that changes with magnitude is a twitch of a different kind:** this surface has a tabular mandate precisely so figures stop moving as they change, and a rendering that switches form at `$9,999 → $10.0k` **re-introduces the instability from the other end, after T82 paid to remove it.** **(3) A cap is a lie about money** — displaying less than he wins is a false factual claim, and a price or a payout is a fact; **C19's *deliberate cap that prints its own count* governs LISTS, never AMOUNTS.** **Also refused and already ruled elsewhere: the figure does not SHRINK** — `tv-design.md` §8's *copy truncates or chooses a shorter authored line, it never shrinks*, and a content-driven size change is the runtime resize §5.1 and §6 both forbid. **What is left is COMPOSITION and SPAN, which is where every other version of this problem landed today.** **Scope, stated so it is not read wider than it is: this governs AMOUNTS** — not counts, ordinals, clocks or scores — and it does not forbid a non-money aggregate elsewhere choosing a compact form on its own ruling | batch 57 |
| C50 | A pinned run pins the DEAL, not the TIMELINE — frame identity is not beat identity | **Law, cross-surface** · DD 2026-08-13 batch 64. **Third catch, and T83 deferred it to exactly this.** **A claim that two frames show the same moment is made against the moment's OWN OBSERVABLE MARKERS — the score, the clock, the event line, the state — never against the filename, the frame index or the seed.** Pinning a run fixes what is dealt; **it does not fix WHEN anything happens**, so frame N of two runs is not the same beat, and a comparison resting on the index **is comparing two different moments while believing it is comparing one.** **THE THREE CATCHES, on three lanes and in BOTH DIRECTIONS: (1)** R43 one lane over — the seed pins the deal, not the timeline (founding mechanism); **(2) T83** — 21 paired frames matched on moment, seed, scene and index and **differing on grammar**, where the README's *"nothing was substituted"* was true and insufficient — **a FALSE PAIRING**; **(3) T95-am** — a clean frame at the same index offered as proof of a fix, on a run that had drifted to a different beat — **a FALSE CONFIRMATION.** **T83 wrote that this promotes on a third catch; this is the third**, and it is the first to arrive as a *confirmation* rather than a *comparison*, **which is what completes the shape: the error is SYMMETRIC and both halves are SILENT.** A drifted frame that looks broken invents a defect; a drifted frame that looks clean retires a real one. **Practical form: a set claiming to show a beat states that beat's MARKERS in its own README**, so a reader checks the claim against the artifact rather than against the naming convention | batch 64 |
| C51 | A cross-element invariant is an ASSERTION or it does not exist | **Law, cross-surface** · DD 2026-08-13 batch 64, promoted from T95. **§3.5's enabling instrument.** **Where two elements are required to hold a relationship — the same rect, the same face, the same value, the same state — that requirement is expressed as a MACHINE-CHECKED ASSERTION, or it is not a requirement at all.** A relationship recorded in prose, in a comment beside the code, or in a reviewer's memory **is UNENFORCED**, and the first ruling that moves one element **breaks it silently and everywhere.** **Founding case:** `Score` is the punch overlay and **its own build comment stated the invariant verbatim** — *"Same text, SAME RECT, same face as `_tMatchup` … so superimposing it"* — yet both centre in their own box; T91-am re-bounded one of them and **the comment could not stop the other from staying where it was**, so the scoreline rendered doubled and illegible on every score change until frames caught it. **TV's own line is the clause's short form: A SHARED LOCAL IS A CONVENTION; AN ASSERTION IS A CONTRACT.** **Why this is a LAW and not a note — it is what makes §3.5 COMPLIABLE:** §3.5 obliges the dependent layout to be re-derived in the same commit as the bound that moved, but **nobody can re-derive a dependency they cannot SEE**, and this one was visible only to a reader of one comment in one file. **A rule requiring perfect recall is a rule that will be broken; C51 converts it into one an instrument keeps.** **Second catch of the same shape, named because it is why this promotes now:** C46-am2 found that **the code knew a worst case and the sweep did not use it** — *a worst case documented in a comment beside the generator is not a worst case the generator uses* — **the same defect class on a different instrument: knowledge recorded where nothing can act on it.** **Both instances are on the TV surface**, so this ships as a register-level law binding all four surfaces by its reasoning and **promotes to the constitution on a catch on a SECOND surface**; this seat does not promote to the constitution on one surface's evidence. **Scope, stated so it is not read wider than it is: this governs INVARIANTS BETWEEN ELEMENTS**, not every design decision — **a ruled value lives in the owning document; a required RELATIONSHIP between two elements lives in a test** | batch 64 |
| C52 | A disclosure block that is not re-verified per dock becomes a false claim | **Law (register-level)** · DD 2026-08-16 batch 97, **promoted from the lane's own correction of its dock template.** **Four earlier docks carried the panel's 0px flush gap as OPEN when it closed at batch 89, and the lane found the MECHANISM rather than the instance: its `NOT CLAIMED` section had become a TEMPLATE, copied between docks without re-checking each line against canon.** **RULED: a disclosure block that is not re-verified per dock stops being a disclosure and becomes a FALSE CLAIM WITH A WIDE READERSHIP.** **Promoted to register level because every dock in this studio carries a `NOT CLAIMED` section and every one is a template in waiting — and the honest-gaps discipline this seat has praised all week is the thing at risk: a stated non-claim is TRUSTED precisely because stating it costs something, and a copied one costs nothing.** **The lane named the four wrong sets explicitly rather than quietly dropping the line** (`…-scorebug-…`, `…-reordered-…`, `…-ticket-keyed-…`, `…-single-count-…`) **so the false line cannot be re-opened from them — the correction done properly.** **It is batch 86's lesson from the other side: that one was *a ruling recorded in a commit message is recorded nowhere a reader looks*; this is *a disclosure copied forward is a claim nobody made*. Both are the artifact drifting from the truth it says it carries, and both are caught by RE-READING rather than by remembering** | batch 97 *(Renumbered `C51` → `C52` and moved from the SureThing table to Cross-surface, 2026-08-16 batch 99 — bookkeeping under C22.1's earlier-ID-governs precedent, authorised on the orchestrator's relay and logged to Allen. Batch 97 promoted this law as `C51`, a number already carried by batch 64's *a cross-element invariant is an ASSERTION or it does not exist*; the C-series ran 1–51 with no gaps, so the collision was silent. The earlier law keeps `C51`. The ruling is untouched — only its number and its table are.)* |
| C53 | A classification with no category for the truth will file the truth under a falsehood | **Law, cross-surface** · DD 2026-08-17 batch 104, **promoted from the consolidated sweep's own §4.2**, which prints `UNACCOUNTED FOR — this number must be 0` and reports **12**. **The twelve stats-panel slots ARE covered** — by the panel's own pin — **but the instrument's only category for a slot it does not sweep is *declared unswept (renders no string)*, which is FALSE for all twelve. The invariant is LYING rather than GAPPING**, and it lies because the taxonomy left it nowhere true to put them. **THE GENERAL FORM: an instrument may report that it did not measure something; it may NOT assert a REASON it has not checked.** A category is a CLAIM, and a default heading applied for want of a better one is a claim made without evidence. **This is not a tooling nicety — it is batch 98 one level up**, where thirteen TV rows sat in the SureThing table because the structure put them where the heading said rather than where they belonged. **THE INSTRUMENT CHANGE, WORDED FOR BUILD — four clauses. (1) A THIRD CATEGORY: `DELEGATED`, meaning covered by a NAMED other instrument.** (2) **It must name that instrument, and the name must RESOLVE — a delegation to a name that does not exist is a lie with extra steps, so the sweep FAILS when the named instrument is absent.** Renaming or deleting a pin must break loudly, because the whole defect being fixed is a silent false claim. **(3) The must-be-zero line does NOT absorb it.** `UNACCOUNTED FOR = 0` stays a hard invariant on its own terms; delegated slots report on their OWN line with their count, their list and the instrument named — **a positive statement, never an absence.** A fix that quiets the alarm by widening what counts as accounted-for is the same defect with better manners. **(4) THE TRAP, AND IT IS THE CLAUSE MOST LIKELY TO BE MISSED: a delegation must distinguish COVERED from SCHEDULED.** *Covered* means the named instrument **has run and docked**. **`T101`'s residual was found in this very window to be "never run and never docked" rather than "no instrument"** — so a `DELEGATED` category that cannot express that would have reported the panel COVERED while it was in fact UNMEASURED, **recreating the identical lie one level higher and inside the fix for it.** **A delegation is a claim with its own staleness and must carry its own evidence date.** | `[TV] TvExtentSweep §4.2 · docs/handoffs/tv-theater.md` |
| C54 | An instrument that reports only the EXTREMUM can find only one defect per subject | **Law, cross-surface** · DD 2026-08-17 batch 110, **promoted from the lane's own reusable finding and it is a better law than the case that produced it.** **`CashOut` was over by 26.7px on `MARKET SUSPENDED` AND by 14.6px on `CASHED OUT $1,240` — and the per-slot sweep could report only the widest, so 267.7 MASKED 255.6.** Fixing the first revealed the second. **The general form: a max-only instrument reports the worst case and is SILENT about every case behind it, so a clean report after a fix means "the widest now fits", never "the box is clear."** **THE PRACTICE THAT FALLS OUT, and it is the useful half: THE SUBJECT MOST WORTH RE-MEASURING IS THE ONE JUST FIXED.** A fix does not only change the thing it touched — **it changes what the instrument can SEE**, and the slot that just lost its widest member is precisely where a second defect has been hiding. **Kin to `C53` and distinct from it:** `C53` is a classification with no category for the truth; **this is a classification with a category that reports only one member.** Both are instruments making claims wider than their evidence. **Also ratified here, same bundle, same class: two sibling instruments (`TvTypeParityProbe` ×2, `TvPromptComposition`) carried the RETIRED string in their own pools and were fixed rather than routed — *a measurement instrument whose pool outlives its string measures a phantom*, which is `T111-am`'s defect caught in two more places on the day it was ruled.** | `[TV] TvExtentSweep · docs/handoffs/tv-theater.md` |
| C55 | A capture gate that asks whether a thing EXISTS will pass on a frame that does not SHOW it | **Law, cross-surface** · DD 2026-08-18 batch 113, **promoted from the markets-pregame lane's self-caught harness fault, which it found, fixed and recorded rather than shipping.** **The founding case: the first shoot PASSED and produced two frames that did not contain their own subjects** — `S3`'s `no prices offered` sat behind fourteen scorer rows below the fold, and `S1`'s PLAYERS line was below the fold. Both assertions used `GetComponentsInChildren`, **which finds objects that have scrolled out of view.** **Three of that set's six states would have docked as evidence of nothing, under a green run.** **THE LAW: EXISTENCE IN THE HIERARCHY IS NOT THE CLAIM A CAPTURE MAKES.** A capture asserts *this frame shows this thing*; a hierarchy query asserts *this thing was constructed*. **They agree exactly until a list scrolls, and then the green run is the lie.** **THE SECOND HALF IS THE ONE THAT WILL BE MISSED — MEASURE IN-FRAME IN LOCAL SPACE, NEVER WORLD SPACE.** The stricter gate then failed twice, correctly: `IsInFrame` first compared **world-space** corners, and **this is a world-space canvas on a physical laptop in a room** — the entire 704px viewport spans about 0.1 world units, so every row rounds together; **and the screen is TILTED, so a world-space horizontal comparison is taken across a rotated plane and means nothing.** It measures in the viewport's **local space — the space the layout is authored in, whose units are the pixels every other constant on this surface is written in.** **KIN TO `C53` AND `C54`, and the family is now three: `C53` a classification with no category for the truth; `C54` an instrument reporting only the extremum; `C55` an instrument asserting the WRONG PREDICATE. All three are instruments making claims wider than their evidence, and all three passed green while doing it.** **The practice: a capture gate names the SUBJECT and asserts it is in frame, and the lists are scrolled to their feet before the shutter.** | `[ST] SureThingVisualCaptureTests · surfaces-evidence-dock-2026-08-18.md` |
| C56 | A SWITCH over a growing enum is a FIXED BOX in a different unit — and every surface's `default` becomes reachable on the same day | **Law (register-level, `C46`/`C39`/`C42`/`C43`'s standing — not proposed for the constitution)** · DD 2026-08-19 batch 123, **promoted from three instances in one week and not from an argument.** **WHERE A SURFACE SWITCHES ON AN ENUM THE ENGINE OWNS, THAT SWITCH CARRIES AN IMPLICIT CLAIM — that its cases cover the enum — AND THE CLAIM IS NEVER WRITTEN DOWN. When the enum grows, EVERY such switch's `default` arm becomes reachable AT THE SAME INSTANT, on every surface, silently.** `C46`'s converse in a different unit: **a fixed box assumes a widest string; a fixed switch assumes a closed enum. Neither assumption is stated and nobody re-derives what they never noticed they declared.** **THE CONSEQUENCE THAT COST THIS STUDIO THE MOST, and it is the half that will be missed: THE SURFACES FAIL DIFFERENTLY, SO FINDING IT ON ONE IS NOT EVIDENCE ABOUT THE OTHERS AND FIXING IT ON ONE CLOSES NOTHING ELSEWHERE.** F_0.5.0 added nine members to `MarketKind`; the laptop's ENTRY went **homeless** (`S86`), the console went **printed-but-unbettable** (`K2`), the TV went **blank-or-enum-name** (`T130`). **Three surfaces, three symptoms, one cause — and each was found separately, weeks apart, by someone looking at that surface for another reason.** **THE TEST, and it is `C46`'s clause (1) transposed: SWEEP THE POPULATION, NOT THE SUSPECTS — after any enum the engine owns gains a member, the set at risk is EVERY SURFACE THAT SWITCHES ON IT, not the one where the defect was noticed.** **AND THE SECOND CLAUSE, from `T130`'s own shape: A `default` THAT RETURNS SOMETHING IS MORE DANGEROUS THAN ONE THAT THROWS.** `LegStatement` falls back to a legacy label and `DescribeActiveLeg` falls back to empty strings — **both ship, neither fails, and a build that prints `CorrectScore` at the player is green.** A `default` arm is a place a surface promises to have thought about a case it has not seen. **Relation to the neighbours: `C19` says a priced offer is reachable; `C56` says the surface that receives it must have WORDS for it — reachability and authorship are two different debts and closing one does not close the other** | batch 123 · precommit §0 |

**IT CANNOT BE THERE.*** **SO THE CAPTURE WOULD HAVE PROVED NOTHING AND WOULD HAVE READ AS A CLEAN RUN** — the worst outcome available, because a green transcript against an unreachable state is the `C55` shape this studio has already paid for twice.** **A SECOND SYMPTOM, FOUND WHILE CHECKING REACHABILITY AND NOT IN `K21`: `onFinalLeg` has a VISIBLE consumer as well as a timing one. `:492-496` prints `"  (the final leg must be sweated — no fast-forward)"` when `F` is pressed on the final leg. **Under the defect that refusal NEVER PRINTS on a same-match ticket's final telling and `F` is silently ACCEPTED** — a STRING-level consequence, which is stronger evidence than timing and is the reason the route below is cheap.** **THE ROUTE THAT SETTLES IT — A GATE, NOT A SHUTTER: `onFinalLeg` is a pure comparison. `lastLeg = ticket.Legs.Count - 1` (`:242`) is the highest leg INDEX; `evt.LegIndex` is now the telling's ANCHOR leg (`DramaEvent.cs:19-21`). **On a two-leg same-match ticket the anchor is leg 0 and `lastLeg` is 1, so `onFinalLeg` is FALSE for every telling of that ticket** — assertable with no rendering, no timing, no terminal and no seed luck, in the console's own exact-gate style (§13: *"every geometric gate here is a string-length assertion, which is exact rather than measured"*). **Mutation-test it the way `K17`'s gate was: restoring the contiguity assumption must fail it.*** **`K21`'s finding is UNCHANGED and is not weakened by this — only its evidence route is** | batch 175 |

| K20 | Two measured corrections to the console spec — one number one low, and one criterion that could never be met because it quoted an ILLUSTRATION | **CORRECTED — DD 2026-08-22 batch 172, on the markets lane's measurements of the built surface, **each re-verified at source here before an Allen-approved spec was edited.*** **(1) §3's LEADER-DOT COUNT WAS ONE LOW — 15, and the surface prints 16. THE CAUSE IS TWO GAP CONVENTIONS FOR ONE DEVICE: `RowGeometry.OfferRow` computes `dots = Field - head.Length - 1`, reserving **ONE** space, while `Page.Leadered` computes `Width - indent - left.Length - 1 - 1 - right.Length`, reserving **TWO**. So an offer row gets one dot more than a contents line for the same content. **THE RULING IS UNTOUCHED — 80 still clears and 62 still fails by one character** — and §6.4's `S100` guard clause is STRENGTHENED rather than weakened: the worst constructible row sits one dot FURTHER from the minimum-run guard than the spec claimed.** **(2) §14's `B4` COULD NOT BE MET AS WRITTEN, and this is the one worth the row. It required *"the folio reading `66–83 of 84`"*. **`Page.BodyRows` is `Height - ChromeRows` = 24 − 4 = 20**, so a first page is ALWAYS 20 offers and PLAYERS paginates `1–20` / `21–40` / … / `81–84`. **`66–83 of 84` cannot occur at any geometry this spec ruled.*** **WHERE THE NUMBER CAME FROM IS THE FINDING: it is §5's own ILLUSTRATIVE example of the folio's FORM, copied forward into the evidence table as a criterion. **THE SPEC QUOTED ITSELF AND TURNED A TEACHING NUMBER INTO A GATE** — and a gate that cannot pass is worse than no gate, because a lane meeting the actual requirement reports a failure against it.** **CORRECTED BOTH WAYS SO IT CANNOT RECUR: `B4` now reads *the folio carrying its OWN range and `[N]ext`, and its next page* — the property, not a value — and **§5's example is marked as an illustration in place**, because a reader at §5 had no way to know it was one.** **THE GENERAL CLAUSE, and it is why this is a row rather than two edits: **AN EXAMPLE IN A PROSE SECTION IS NOT A SPECIFICATION.** This register has ruled the neighbouring shapes — `C58-am` (a docstring is not a measurement), `T154` (a stated caveat is not a check), `P9` (a comment about a file is not the file) — and this is the same family: **a number printed to show the SHAPE of a thing, read later as the VALUE of it.** `B4`'s pin was met throughout; only the criterion was wrong.** **NEITHER CORRECTION TOUCHES A RULING, NO EVIDENCE IS INVALIDATED, AND `B4` IS SATISFIED. The spec's amendments are marked in place with their cause and their date** | batch 172 |
