C46 DISCHARGED rather than merely satisfied — the box is safe and the reason is legible to whoever changes the model next.** **One residual, and it is this seat's question that was one-sided rather than the lane's answer: American odds grow in BOTH directions and I asked only for the maximum — the same shape as the payout-arithmetic slip one batch earlier, asking for one bound of a two-sided quantity.** Structurally moot (a negative price needs the draw priced more likely than not) **but named anyway, because this seat ruled the same morning that a plausibility argument about a model the surface does not own is not a measurement — and that applies to its own.** **Asked, not ordered; it closes either way.** Full text: `register-entries-2026-08-15-batch-82.md`

- **Batch 83 (2026-08-15) — written at the DD seat — S84's RESIDUAL CLOSES, from the existing sweep with no run spent.** **The minimum reachable draw price is decimal 3.3527 and is ATTAINED, where 4.2058 is a supremum** — `+235` against `+320`, **three digits at both ends, and tabular digits make every string between them identical**, so the cell sits at 87% for every price the model can emit. **No negative American price exists; batch 82 reasoned that structurally and called its own reasoning insufficient, and it is now measured.** Corroborated by every frame this seat has read, all interior to the bound — **the observed sample sitting inside the measured population is what a correct bound looks like from the outside.** **The lane's caveat earned a rule, and it is this surface's third arrival at it from a third direction:** one end is attained and the other is not, so listing them as a matched pair would quietly claim the board can print a price it cannot. At the face the distinction is immaterial — **the surface never meets the decimal, it meets `+320`** — **but that is a consequence, not a licence.** **RULED: pin what is RENDERED, never what is REACHABLE in the model** — as the DRAW cell's gate already measures rendered cells rather than constants, and as C46's widths came off the rendered control rather than the call site. **A boundary in the model is not a boundary on the face until it has been through the formatter**, which also lets the supremum/attained distinction be recorded honestly without ever being reproduced in a test. Full text: `register-entries-2026-08-15-batch-83.md`

- **Batch 84 (2026-08-15) — written at the DD seat — S83 IS DESIGN-VERIFIED, and the README under-claimed its own evidence in the one place that mattered.** **The clause C was argued on holds on the frame:** on a slip overrunning by 24.1px, `STAKE $35`, the chips, the nudges, `POTENTIAL PAYOUT`, **`$2,009` with its wax band** and `PLACE TICKET` are all anchored and in shot — **S17/S73's *cost he cannot see at the point of spending*, answered structurally rather than by hoping the content is short.** **But the README called the rail *"effectively invisible at this render scale"*, and measured it is x 1020–1023 at luminance ~105 with a thumb of 157px against a predicted 156.7 — the SAME contrast as the board's rail this seat measured the same morning.** **A lane under-claiming its own evidence is still a mis-statement of evidence, and this one nearly cost the read**, because the read turns on which channel carries the signal and the README named the wrong one. **`S83-am3` CLOSES: the seam's ink clearance measures 6px against a floor of ≥6px — at the boundary rather than comfortably, which is why batch 81 made it a gate.** **And the finding: the clipped fragment is ANONYMOUS — a pale featureless bar under the `COMBINED` rule — so S81-am's *the cut block is its own signal* DOES NOT TRANSFER, because the board's clipped content was self-identifying and a chip's blank top is not.** **Accepted anyway: the rail carries the signal, the fragment states nothing false, no remedy exists that does not break §2's derived-not-chosen rule, and the anonymity belongs to the state rather than the design.** **`S85`: the dead click at MaxLegs is a defect by §8 — a price cell is an offer, an offer that cannot be taken is not an offer, and a control that accepts a click and does nothing states something it will not honour.** **Ruled generally, because the gesture will make more of this class: where a refusal is knowable BEFORE the act the surface shows it before and the act never happens; where it is knowable only after, the stamp states cause and remedy. A dead click is a knowable refusal left to be discovered.** **One trap named — reusing `frozen`'s dim would give two causes one appearance (S2) — and the treatment is NOT ruled without a frame, having declined all day to verify reads without one.** Full text: `register-entries-2026-08-15-batch-84.md`

- **Batch 85 (2026-08-15) — written at the DD seat — T99 CLOSES: all four checks PASS, and the ruling's standing condition earned its keep within hours of being written.** **The overlay's bottom edge is a structural line rather than a stopping point; no fragment of the scorebug survives; the `GOALS` row reads as a table row and not a scoreline (checked and CLEARED: the panel's column order matches the TICKET column's backed-side-first convention, not the scorebug's neutral record, and both already coexisted); and the clock ran 16′→18′, held 18′ across THIRTY contiguous frames, then resumed FROM 18′ with no catch-up.** **Stopped and continued, not paused-and-caught-up.** **THE MOST VALUABLE THING IN THE SET IS THAT THE FIRST RUN FAILED:** its own log disproved its claim — the minute ticked `18′ → 21′` behind the panel — because `TickClock` read `Time.deltaTime` while the `!_seated` guard was what actually froze it: **two expressions of one rule agreeing by convention, so a third freeze condition never reached the clock.** **PROMOTED, the lane's formulation and better than this seat's: *a channel that never reads the authority is invisible to a pin on the authority.*** **And the standing condition is what made that a failure rather than a shipped frame — a ruling written as *approved* instead of *approved while X holds* would have passed it.** **The event-strip question was answered before the shoot and correctly: the strip is not covered, pinned as non-overlap against live rects.** **Also shipped: `T100`, the panel's composition RAISED but not ruled** — it is largely empty, but two of three rows show their unrevealed form off a moneyline leg, **and a surface shot in its emptiest state cannot be read for how it fills; one frame with a populated count row is owed first.** **`T101`: the `TAB` key docketed to Allen with T88's `ENTER` precedent, and the panel's own strings named as un-swept under C46.** Full text: `register-entries-2026-08-15-batch-85.md`

- **Batch 86 (2026-08-15) — written at the DD seat — `T101` CLOSES: `TAB` ratified by Allen.** TV's pick stands, **and the lane was right to flag it rather than assume it** — a panel toggle is its own act and `ENTER` being the studio commit key does not extend to it. Nothing blocked on it; the panel ships unchanged. **One line recorded on how it arrived, because it is the THIRD claim-vs-artifact gap this seat caught today: batch 85 landed with a commit message saying *"TAB ratified by Allen and recorded"* while both the batch file and the register row still read *docketed, unratified*.** No harm done and none implied — the relay was correct and the ruling is Allen's either way — **but with batch 73 sitting unlanded while a docket asked for work already on disk, and a README calling a rail invisible that measured at the same contrast as one verified hours earlier, the pattern is worth naming: A RULING RECORDED IN A COMMIT MESSAGE IS RECORDED NOWHERE A READER LOOKS. Canon lives in the register and the owning doc; a message describes a change, it does not make one.** Batch 68's own lesson in a fourth place. **Recorded, not routed — nobody needs to do anything except keep writing rulings into the files.** Full text: `register-entries-2026-08-15-batch-86.md`

- **Batch 87 (2026-08-15) — written at the DD seat — THE DEAD CLICK RULED ON ITS FRAME, AND THE PANEL'S DEAD SPACE IS STRUCTURAL.** **`S85`: eighteen prices on a full board — four ringed, FOURTEEN DEAD, and not one says so**; `05 MALLARDS · AWAY +239` renders exactly as the picked matchups did before they were picked. **The control stops offering and the cause is stated ONCE — fourteen dead cells are one fact about the slip, not fourteen facts about prices, and a refusal on every refused control would put more words on the board than it has prices.** **§8 supplies the treatment: a price cell is both a FACT (the house's line) and an OFFER (a thing he may take), and at the cap it is still true and no longer takeable — so the offer affordance goes and the price stays legible.** **`frozen`'s dim may not be reused, and the meanings say why: frozen DIMS THE FACT (the round is locked), the cap REMOVES THE OFFER (the price is still true) — one treatment for both would teach him a full slip is a closed round.** **The inversion is accepted — at the cap the only live cells are the ringed ones, which is the state agreeing with biro's existing meaning, not a second meaning loaded onto the mark.** **Scope clause: every market behind every `MORE ›` is dead on the same terms, so a treatment covering only the board's price cells leaves the defect everywhere the frame does not look.** **`T100`: the populated count row answers the reserved question AGAINST the panel — `CORNERS 2 | 1` is real content and the panel is as empty as it was, because the table is three rows in every state and the panel is sized to the SCREEN.** **Ruled: sized once at design time to what it carries — §2's own legal move.** **A surface that takes the entire stage and returns three rows has not earned the stage** — and this is not a complaint about empty space, which this studio has twice ruled correct; **the objection is the EXCHANGE.** **One coupling named for TV: if a resized panel no longer covered the scorebug, T99's conditional licence would not be needed at all.** Full text: `register-entries-2026-08-15-batch-87.md`

- **Batch 88 (2026-08-15) — written at the DD seat — THE PANEL DROPS CLEAR OF THE SCOREBUG (Allen, B), and the owning doc says the extent clause was never changed, only RESTORED.** **The coupling batch 87 named lands exactly as named: T99's licence goes moot, the freeze survives on its own clause, and the player keeps the score.** **The phrase folded: *"the head of the ticket column"* → *"the ticket column"*, because a phrase that names a SEAM goes stale every time the seam moves while one that names a RELATIONSHIP does not** — the DRAW cell's midpoint one surface over. **AND THE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE ACCOUNT: §6.6 has always read *it expands over the column and stage* — two regions, and the scorebug is a THIRD. The doc never licensed covering it; the shipped panel did anyway; Allen's placement returns the panel inside a line already drawn.** **Stated plainly rather than routed: T99 answered TV's question without noticing the owning doc had already spoken — a ruling granting what the document already refused, cycle 220's own defect, from the seat that keeps citing it. What kept the cost at zero is that T99 was ruled CONDITIONALLY, and that condition is what failed the first shoot and caught the unfrozen clock; a flat approval would have granted the overreach permanently and caught nothing.** **T99 is MOOT but DORMANT, not retired — if the panel is ever raised back over the band it applies again and its condition binds.** **And §6.6's standing *ships at authored height with no reserved space* (T21) means batch 87's sizing ruling was never new: the panel shipped at screen height against a clause already binding, so the resize is a RETURN to canon rather than a change of it.** Full text: `register-entries-2026-08-15-batch-88.md`; folded into `tv-design.md` §6.6

- **Batch 89 (2026-08-15) — written at the DD seat — T100 CLOSES: the resize is verified, and three things ride with it.** **The panel drops to 29.5% of its area with boxes derived from a committed sweep, and the scorebug pin is the right SHAPE — full 2D non-overlap, deliberately not single-axis, so a change narrowing only the vertical gap is still caught as the partial coverage it would be.** **The now-vacuous freeze guard was KEPT, correctly: it is written where a future re-enlargement would be made, and deleting a guard because it currently guards nothing is how the T95 class recurs.** **`T100-am2`: TV flagged the 0px flush edge as possibly reading *attached* — measured, the panel's field is ~24–26 against ~23 outside, TWO TO THREE luminance units, so there is no visible boundary to attach with. An edge that cannot be seen cannot read as attached; no gap ordered.** **But the finding underneath is real and is now written: the panel's presence is carried entirely by OCCLUSION — it reads because the pitch stops at it, not because a panel is drawn — so neither a gap nor a border should be added on this frame, and a change that removes the occlusion would leave nothing to read at all.** **`T102`: `contentMargin = 16` NOT ratified as a constant — C46's risk is proportional, so a fixed pixel margin gives its least protection on the widest string (`MATCH STATS` survives a face ~10% wider and overflows at 11%). S77-am already rules this hazard at *under 80%*, and C46 is a cross-surface law: inventing a second headroom budget for the same hazard is one-name-per-thing broken at the level of RULES. Ink ≤ 80% of box; the panel goes ~564 → ~613, still 37% of the original.** **And S84 binds the value column — team names are GENERATED, so the box sizes against the enumerated pool's widest, not the sweep's widest measured.** **`T103`: the placement changed what justifies the GOALS row.** **T99 ruled it legitimate WHILE the panel covered the scorebug; now the score is never covered, so the row duplicates it two slots down — and in OPPOSITE column order, which T99 cleared explicitly because the two never coexisted.** **At 2–1 the screen would read `YAMS 2 — 1 ZAMBONIS` above and `Zambonis 1 | Yams 2` below.** **And this set cannot show it, because it is 0–0 — the same trap T99's own capture condition was written to avoid.** Three options to Allen; **(b) reorder now, (c) key the rows to the ticket when the panel is next opened; (a) deleting the row alone answers the composition and worsens the product.** Full text: `register-entries-2026-08-15-batch-89.md`

- **Batch 90 (2026-08-15) — written at the DD seat — `T103` RULED (b) by Allen: the panel's columns take the scorebug's order.** The mirror that could actively mislead is closed by one reordering; the duplication remains and is accepted for now; **(c), keying the panel's rows to the ticket it opens from, stays recorded for the panel's next content opening.** **One consequence written down so it is not later filed as a defect: aligning the panel to the scorebug UN-aligns it from the ticket column — the very pairing this seat used at T99 to clear the reversal. The trade is the right way round for a reason that survives the change: the ticket column's progress line is a SENTENCE, not a two-column table.** *`LEADING 1–0`* **names no team and reads from the backed side's perspective, so it has no column order to disagree with and cannot mirror; the scorebug can, presenting the same two teams in two columns of digits one slot away.** **The alignment goes where a mirror is possible, and the surface it leaves behind cannot produce one — only one of the two pairings was ever capable of the defect.** **And the reorder's own frame wants a NON-LEVEL scoreline: a 0–0 set cannot show a column order to be right any more than it could show it wrong.** Full text: `register-entries-2026-08-15-batch-90.md`

- **Batch 91 (2026-08-16) — written at the DD seat — S85's TREATMENT GRANTED ON ITS FRAMES, and ENTRY's missing channel ruled closed.** **The field is removed and the type untouched: measured, the ringed cell's field is −9.0 before and −9.0 after while the bare cells go −7.6 → −1.7 and −9.7 → −3.5, with no type dimmed anywhere.** **IT IS NOT A NEW RULE, IT IS S69's** — *a disabled LOCK is TRANSPARENT, it carried a fill and no border* — **so §7's *no code he must learn* is answered by there being nothing new to learn at all.** **And the `frozen` distinction turned out ORTHOGONAL rather than merely different: frozen dims the TYPE and keeps the field, the cap keeps the TYPE and removes the field, so the two can co-occur without ambiguity. §7 asked for distinguishable and got independent.** **The cause is the DENOMINATOR — `4 OF 4 SELECTIONS` — and the remedy is present as CONTROLS rather than words, the `RUB OUT`s live beside the count, so cause-and-remedy is satisfied without a sentence.** **`S85-am`: the lane was right to refuse to invent a field — that manufactures a distinction in order to destroy it.** **The gap's precise shape, derived here from source: `MakeOfferRow` already carries a `selected` state and the kit gives the ring alone the biro, so ENTRY separates *yours* from *not yours* and cannot separate *available* from *unavailable*.** **And that category is NEW — before the gesture every unringed offer was always takeable, so the kit was complete for the world it was drawn in and the gesture created a state the sheet was never built to express.** **CLOSED on two grounds: the click is refused before it happens on both surfaces, and the cause is on screen there — verified at source, `BuildSlip` is called from BOTH `BuildLobby` and `BuildDetail`, so *stated once* is satisfied on both surfaces by one statement.** **Neither reachable case is ambiguous; the residual is named with its trigger and goes to Allen as a kit deviation if it ever becomes live.** Full text: `register-entries-2026-08-16-batch-91.md`

- **Batch 92 (2026-08-16) — written at the DD seat — T103 AND T102 VERIFIED ON ONE SET, and the 0.7px flag is the distance to the ALARM rather than to the failure.** **The reorder: both axes agree on the frame, and the order is now written at the panel's site as *the scorebug's*, citing the composition line, so the two cannot be chosen independently again — the FOURTH derivation-instead-of-value this week, which has stopped being a correction and become how this studio builds.** **And it was fixed on EVERY row together, because swapping the headers alone would have put the right names over the wrong numbers — a state lie, and one that would have passed a casual look.** **T102: 195/145, panel 613, area 32.1%, one named `MaxInkFraction` with both widths derived and `contentMargin` removed rather than left dead.** **S84's pool binding now GATES over 20 enumerated clubs and is deliberately NOT `[Explicit]` — the C46 sweep is filter-only and never runs routinely, which is precisely how a 21st club could have overflowed unnoticed; a binding that only runs when someone remembers to run it is not a binding.** **And it reads `MaxInkFraction` off production rather than restating it, so test and surface cannot disagree.** **`T102-am`: THREE NUMBERS AND ONLY ONE IS 0.7 — ink 115.3, gate limit 116.0 (0.7px to the ALARM), box 145.0 (29.7px to the OVERFLOW). The gate fires 29.7px before anything breaks, which is what an early-warning pin is for; the 20% is a FACE budget and is fully intact. DO NOT PAD THE BOX TO QUIET THE ALARM — that spends the face budget to buy pool slack, mixing two budgets, which is what rejecting `contentMargin` was about.** **`T100-am3`: the widening cost a piece of the stage, measured — the right edge moved x≈1452 → x≈1551 and now covers the centre circle's left arc. Licensed by §6.6 and accepted, and the right edge is a CONSEQUENCE of the ink budget, never a target: tuning the width to clear the circle would size a zone to its neighbour rather than its content.** **The offsetting half was not aimed at — the panel reads by occlusion, so occluding more means it reads better as an object than it did at 564.** Full text: `register-entries-2026-08-16-batch-92.md`

- **Batch 93 (2026-08-16) — written at the DD seat — (c) RULED: THE PANEL IS THE PER-TEAM SPLIT OF THE COUNTS THE TICKET RIDES ON.** **The subject had to be settled before the rows could follow, and settling it named what three surfaces each own: the SCOREBUG gives the result, the TICKET COLUMN gives each leg's progress toward its line, and the panel gives the per-team BREAKDOWN neither can — which is what *opens from the ticket column* has meant all along and was never true of its content.** **Row set: one row per countable quantity the ticket rides on, deduped — the unit is the QUANTITY, not the leg — in a fixed canonical order, so the ticket selects WHICH rows appear and never in what order.** **`T104-am`: THE GOALS ROW IS REMOVED, and the argument is STRUCTURAL rather than a duplication complaint — the panel exists to give the SPLIT, and for goals there is no split to give: the panel's two numbers and the scorebug's are the same two, in the same order, one slot apart. There is nothing to ADD, not merely something repeated — and that holds however the panel is keyed, which is why (c) did not dissolve it on its own.** **Every goals market is served by the scorebug directly, so removing the row costs no fact; a scorer leg takes no row by the same rule rather than a special case.** **THE CONSEQUENCE STATED PLAINLY: a moneyline-only ticket gives the panel nothing, and the panel does not open empty — its affordance is unavailable and says so BEFORE the key is pressed, which is S85's law made on the laptop three batches ago, applied on a second surface. (c) therefore makes the panel a COUNT-TICKET feature, available where it has something to say, which is also the honest answer to batch 87's scope question.** **And the unrevealed mark SURVIVES and changes meaning — where `—` means *not in your ticket* today, under (c) it means *your ticket rides on this and it is not revealed yet*: the mark stops meaning IRRELEVANT and starts meaning NOT YET.** **§2 is satisfied and the reasoning recorded: the row set is derived once at placement, cannot change under the player, and has no siblings to be ragged against — the draws block had siblings, the panel has none.** **`T105`: `MATCH STATS` now overstates its subject and is COUPLED to the box, since it is the widest ink setting `labelW`; flagged for the lane to author, not changed in passing.** Full text: `register-entries-2026-08-16-batch-93.md`

- **Batch 94 (2026-08-16) — written at the DD seat — THE STATS PHASE CLOSES: four items in one read.** **`T104-am2`: the blank-row consequence is real, and two thirds of it is a ruling not yet built** — `GOALS 0 | 0` is on the frame, and batch 93 removed that row *not conditionally, not keyed*; with both unbuilt clauses in, **a moneyline ticket has NO PANEL AT ALL and the "one row in a three-row panel" case does not exist.** **Batch 87's *earned the stage* finding does not reopen — it reopens only against a build that kept a row the ruling removed.** **The residual is a BUILD defect: absent and unrevealed rows are different states and the build conflates them — a row never bought should have no slot, a row bought but unrevealed keeps its slot and carries the mark.** **Ruled: the height follows the row set, derived at adoption from a computation that already exists, so (i) is cheaper than priced; (ii) is right for absent rows and backwards in the build; (iii) leaves a defect rather than a cost.** **`T105` RULED `COUNTS`** — and **the coupling has a FLOOR TV's table does not show: `labelW` must hold `CORNERS` too, so a title shorter than ~99px buys nothing and the panel bottoms out near 542.** `COUNTS` is the surface's own word, sits in the label column's header cell where the natural content is what the row labels ARE, drops `STATS`'s false breadth, and matches every other label's register — **and it deliberately does NOT caption the ticket connection, because §3.1's mark is DRAWN, not CAPTIONED.** **`T100-am2` CLOSED and restated** — ruled at batch 89, carried forward as *still open* across three docks; **a ruling that keeps being re-listed as open is a ruling that did not reach its reader, batch 86's lesson from the other direction.** **`T106`: the composition GRANTED — the frame shows a row with a number beside a row saying *not yet*, which is the mark's meaning shift rendered rather than argued, and the lane's retention store (found by building) prevents a revealed fact un-revealing itself.** Full text: `register-entries-2026-08-16-batch-94.md`

- **Batch 95 (2026-08-16) — written at the DD seat — THE TITLE IS VERIFIED AND IT CORRECTED THIS SEAT TWICE; the phase does not close.** **`COUNTS` on the frame: `labelW` 195 → 111, panel 613 → 529, area down to 27.7% of the original.** **It corrected my estimate — I predicted a ~99px floor and a ~542px panel against a measured 88.5 and 529 — AND I WAS WRONG FOR A REASON I DID NOT SEE: the column holds strings at TWO type sizes, and I scaled `MATCH STATS`'s per-character width as though one governed. That is the exact error class this seat spent the week ruling against, recorded against myself.** **The lane's generalisation is promoted: *the widest string in a column is a MEASUREMENT, never something readable off string lengths or type sizes* — a 15px row label came within 7.3px of overtaking a 19px title.** **Both sides corrected on measurement, which is the standard working.** **A bonus nobody claimed: at 529 the centre circle is WHOLE again, so `T100-am3`'s accepted cost is partly repaid — the title work paid back a cost a different ruling had accepted, because both are consequences of the same budget.** **BUT THE PHASE DOES NOT CLOSE: `GOALS | 0 | 0` is still on the frame (second dock in a row), the absent row is still a blank SLOT, and the height is unchanged at 246 — three of four criteria unbuilt.** **This seat takes its share: batch 94 said *all four as one change* and then *one frame closes it*, and the second sentence should have said the frame comes AFTER the change.** **The build's blank-versus-mark distinction is real and is KEPT — but batch 94's point was the SLOT: a blank slot still occupies a row while saying nothing, so the two are complementary and an unbought row should be NO row.** **The closing criterion is binary: a corners-only ticket makes the panel ONE ROW TALL.** Full text: `register-entries-2026-08-16-batch-95.md`

- **Batch 96 (2026-08-16) — written at the DD seat — `GOALS` STAYS (Allen); two rows is right.** **Batch 93's removal is overruled and not re-argued. TV caught the contradiction with the keying rule and ASKED rather than building through it, which is what got the question in front of him.** **THE FORMULATION THAT MAKES THE TWO RULES AGREE: `GOALS` is a STANDING row, not a keyed one — the panel is `GOALS` plus the count rows the ticket keys, and keying governs what sits BENEATH it. The contradiction was that batch 93 applied keying to a row that was never keyed.** **Recorded BEFORE the closing shot because two already-routed items die with the removal: the ZERO-ROW AFFORDANCE is moot and withdrawn (the panel is never empty now, and an outstanding obligation that can no longer fire is a thing someone eventually builds), and the "count-ticket feature" framing is withdrawn.** **Surviving unchanged: the keying rule, absent-rows-no-slot, unrevealed-rows-keep-their-slot-and-mark, height-follows-rows, and `COUNTS` — whose justification is unchanged in substance and in fact reads TRUER with the row in, since goals, corners and cards are all counts.** **T103's duplication, accepted at batch 90, is now permanent rather than provisional.** **One consequence stated once and not argued: a moneyline ticket now yields a one-row panel carrying `GOALS` alone — the ruling was made on the corners case, and the moneyline case follows without having been the thing decided.** **Closing criterion restated: a corners-only ticket makes the panel EXACTLY TWO ROWS with no blank beneath, superseding batch 95's *one row tall*.** Full text: `register-entries-2026-08-16-batch-96.md`

- **Batch 97 (2026-08-16) — written at the DD seat — THE STATS PHASE CLOSES.** **The criterion is met and measured at this seat rather than read off the log: the panel's bottom edge moves y 792 → 691 against the predecessor, a 101px reduction that is EXACTLY ONE 46px ROW PITCH at this frame's scale — the panel shrank by one ROW, not by a number someone chose — and a pitch feature now reads where the panel covered it, so the stage is given back measurably.** **The absent signal is distinct from the mark at the source, so the lane's blank-versus-mark distinction is kept and now sits UNDERNEATH a slot distinction rather than substituting for it.** **One formula, one application site, called at ticket adoption; 246 stops being a fixed value and becomes a maximum.** **And the lane caught a second-order defect inside its own fix — unused slots are collapsed onto the last active row rather than hidden in place, which would have left the very hole the ruling is about AND quietly broken the symmetry pin that reads inactive children. A fix that passes its own gate by accident is the failure this studio spent the week naming.** **`C52` PROMOTED** *(promoted at this batch as `C51`, renumbered to `C52` at batch 99 on the silent collision with batch 64's law — the ruling is untouched)* **from the lane's correction of its own dock template: four docks carried a closed item as open because the `NOT CLAIMED` section had become a template copied without re-checking — *a disclosure block that is not re-verified per dock stops being a disclosure and becomes a false claim with a wide readership.* Register-level, because every dock here carries one and every one is a template in waiting; and a stated non-claim is trusted precisely because stating it costs something.** **Batch 86's lesson from the other side, and both are caught by re-reading rather than remembering.** **PHASE TOTAL: panel `980 × 480` → `529 × 200`, 22.5% of where it began; the scorebug never covered; rows keyed to the ticket under a standing `GOALS`; height derived at adoption; `MATCH STATS` → `COUNTS`; and the unrevealed mark moved from *not in your ticket* to *not yet revealed*.** Full text: `register-entries-2026-08-16-batch-97.md`

- **Batch 98 (2026-08-16) — written at the DD seat — BOOKKEEPING: THE CANON PAGE WAS LOSING 75 OF 343 ROWS, and the misfiled stats phase was the smaller half of it.** **No design ruling is made, amended or reopened in this batch.** **The mechanism: a blank line TERMINATES a GFM table, and 39 had accumulated between rows — so every row after the first blank in a section was not a table row at all, but a literal paragraph of pipe-delimited text with no header above it.** Measured with cmark-gfm, the library GitHub renders with, rather than asserted: **75 rows not rendering → 0; SureThing 38 of 120 → 0; TV 37 of 115 → 0; 40 pipe-prose paragraphs → 0.** **Everything from `S51-cl` onward on the laptop, and the whole late TV run, was off the canon page** — C22's *the tables are the canon* failing at the only layer that matters, and the second render-level defect in two days. **The repair is whitespace ONLY and it is proved, not claimed: the multiset of non-blank lines is byte-identical before and after.** **`T99`–`T106` (thirteen rows) MOVED to the TV table**, appended after `T98` in authored order, **every ID unchanged under C22.1 on the `C43` precedent (batch 34)** — the cost of the misfiling was that the TV table ended at `T98`, so **a TV lead reading their own table found nothing about the panel that had just shipped.** SureThing 120 → 107, TV 115 → 128;
